skill: Convert a positive numerical radical to the same radicand raised to the unit fractional exponent reciprocal to its root index.
learner_operation: Read the radicand and root index (implicit 2 for square roots), preserve the radicand as base, and place the index in the denominator under numerator 1; distinguish swapped and inverted assignments among five radio choices.
reasoning_steps: Identify x and n in sqrt[n]{x}.
Treat an unindexed square root as n=2.
Form x^(1/n), select its equivalent choice, and explain using the radical/exponent identity.
response_contract: Observed assessed questions use one five-choice math radio field selection. Canonical example has no captured answer field.
difficulty: easy; one direct notation conversion, positive small integer radicand and integer root index, no power-law composition.
invariants: Radical to unit fractional exponent direction.
One numerical radical; no added algebra or multi-step simplification.
Correct expression preserves radicand and uses reciprocal root index.
Five radio math options with exactly one correct answer for captured question profiles.
permitted_variations: Vary positive radicand and index while avoiding duplicate/equivalent distractors.
Include implicit square-root and explicit indexed-root cases.
Vary which numeral is radicand versus index; the source examples do not justify fixing their magnitude ordering.
Permute correct choice position and distractor presentation; alternative same-skill distractor profiles require checking for structural cues.
Vary the three observed prompt wordings without changing required reasoning.
